hook: SCP-209 is a chipped whisky tumbler that never runs dry until someone drinks from it, and its effect needs an audience: one drinker and at least one bystander. The rules are laid out like a checklist before the article shows them in action. The test log at the end describes two people dying slowly and painfully while a third watches in good spirits.
whyItMatters:
The article is a neat study in how one simple premise, the way someone describes a drink, can be turned into a weapon. Tasting words that would be idle praise at a bar become the mechanism of harm, which gives the file a very particular kind of cruelty.

It also shows how much a containment section can carry on its own. The locker that shuts down when two people approach it and the filters against an enticing smell tell you the shape of the danger before the description does.
thingsToNotice:
Whoever smells it first and drinks becomes the Activator, and everyone else within twenty metres is pinned between two invisible walls, unable to get closer than a metre or farther than twenty. In the log, the drinker calls the Scotch smoky and one subject coughs black smoke until he dies; he calls it smooth and the other sweats a slick fluid that strips away layers of skin, begs to be killed, is refused, and dies too. The drinker applauds now and then.

The last beat is the most telling one. Once the glass is empty, the Activator rushes to a corpse and tries to refill it with blood, so the cycle only ends because security steps in. It is worth rereading the early note that the drink is highly addictive and is best treated with methadone, because this scene is that craving shown in action.
